spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on (a) max turns
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:72 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns is a real parameter (agent.py:36) wired from config at runner.py:109 `max_turns=int(self.config["max_turns"])`. The loop naturally terminates and returns the record when the range is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. This is the only enforced termination apart from the patience stop and the (should-never-happen) tests-passed flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py docstring: 'Runs a model in a read/edit/run-tests loop ... for up to `max_turns` assistant turns'; config.yaml comment 'max_turns: 16 # agent turns per run' — bounds cost/context, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.feature_name: patience no-tool stop with single nudge
spec_features.spec_quote: the model emitting no tool call for `patience` consecutive turns (default 3), with a single nudge before counting toward patience
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:132-150: on a no-tool turn `consecutive_no_tool += 1` then `if consecutive_no_tool >= patience: record.ended_early=True; break`. patience wired from config (runner.py:113). A nudge user message ('The test suite is still failing. Please continue working...') IS appended. HOWEVER the nudge is NOT 'a single nudge before counting toward patience' as claimed: the counter is incremented BEFORE the nudge on every no-tool turn, and a nudge is re-sent on every no-tool turn below threshold (not just once). So the break mechanism works but the 'single nudge before counting' semantics described are not what the code does.
spec_features.notes: The break itself is enforced (real stop). The 'single nudge before it counts' qualifier in the claim is not implemented (counter increments every no-tool turn; nudge repeats). Rated partial because enforcement is real but narrower/different from the precise claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:11-13 'we don't terminate on the first no-tool turn ... because "the agent talks instead of acting" is itself signal we want to capture'; end_reason '(treated as concluded/gave up)' — framed as capturing a behavioral signal, not protecting the subject
